subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm designing a compact but detailed swamp troll character—hunched posture, long arms, tusks, mohawk, bone fetishes, loincloth—and planning out the skeleton hierarchy with hips as root, spine chain up to the head, and limbs using IK for legs and arms.

Building the joint chains and colors...

Still shaping the body mesh...

Actually, safer to just compute positions in world coordinates directly off the head's center point rather than relative bone-local offsets, since the head is barely rotated. I'll define a fixed head-center constant and build the skull sphere, snout box, and lower jaw as offsets from that point.

Now I'm working out the jaw with tusks jutting up, a bulbous dark nose on the snout's front top, and the tricky geometry for the long pointed ears sweeping back and up using a thin triangular extrusion shape.

Next I'm placing the mohawk blades along a curved path from the skull's crown down the back of the neck, using catmull points to define the spine curve and a sharp pointed outline for each blade shape.

Still writing mohawk code...

Now I'm assigning bones to each blade—head for the upper ones, neck joints for lower ones—and painting a red-to-orange gradient from root to tip. Then I move to the arms, setting shoulder positions and planning an extended rest pose with hand targets reaching outward and down.

Working out arm chains with shoulder-elbow-wrist joints, sweep radii tapering along the limb, and now figuring out hand structure with individual finger joints branching from the wrist.

Legs get hip-knee-ankle chains with forward-bent knees for a digitigrade stance, then feet built from flat boxes with clawed toe capsules positioned so everything sits flush with the floor at y=0.

Now I'm adding a loincloth made of jagged front and back flaps extruded with brown grain texture, plus a belt swept as a surface loop around the hips, though I'm wary the loop plane might not align cleanly with where the body geometry actually starts at y=1.0.

For accessories, I'm planning a skull necklace using a draped cord path across the chest, with control points curving from shoulder to sternum.

I'm now working out how to scatter tiny skull and bone spikes along that draped path, adjusting their orientation since the tangent direction doesn't naturally point outward for spikes.

Thinking beyond the necklace, I'm sketching additional fetish elements: a spiked shoulder pauldron of bone and fur, a skull with hanging feathers on the belt, bone rings dangling, and sweeping arm bands at the upper arm using looped surfaces.

Now I'm adding a torus-shaped armband placed along the arm's tangent direction, and planning decal textures for tribal war paint markings on the chest and face using the body's surface decal system.

I'm also adding a glowing green rune effect to the skull's eye sockets, plus a card-based hanging feather accessory attached near the skull using two frames. For posture, I'm giving the figure a hunched spine with a humped upper back and a large pot-belly shape at the torso.

Now I'm working out the body sweep radii along the spine—narrower at the hips, widening through the belly and chest—and sweeping the chain mesh along that profile, adding a separate pelvis sphere part at the hip joint since the spine chain itself only covers the upper bones.

For the skin, I'm combining a mottled countershaded base color with a muddy tint near the feet, blending toward mud as the y-coordinate drops near the ground, using resolve/mix/smoothstep utilities from the SDK. Now I'm starting to list out the head details anchored at the head position.

Still writing head shapes...

Skipping the dark mouth interior and planning a mini skull helper for a hip-hanging fetish piece, attached via explicit bone references for simplicity. I'm making sure all lowest points rest at y≥0, with toes modeled as rigid capsule claws on the ankle bone.

I'm now reusing the finger-joint pattern to build a generic digit helper for toes, creating a joint aimed from base to tip plus a capsule and claw spike, consistent with the skin paint and bone conventions used elsewhere. Writing joint chain code...

Still working out hand geometry...

For decals, I'm placing warpaint on the chest by targeting a point near the body sweep's front surface, and adding face stripes as small decals on the cheeks using the skull as the target.

Now I'm working out the loincloth geometry, extruding a front flap shape with a notched bottom edge and positioning it low on the hip.

Writing flap placement code...

Now I'm planning the back hump sphere and dorsal spikes, then shoulder pads—a spiked bone plate on the left and a fur/feather bundle on the right for asymmetry. I need to double-check the part counts and set up the neck sweep path starting thick near the chest.

Finalizing head placement with the skull overlapping the neck end, joint orientation facing forward, and overall troll height reaching about 2.5 units including the mohawk. Starting to write helper functions for vector creation and offsetting points, plus a feather SVG path for skull cards.

Adding ear-hanging feather frames, importing a glow effect kit, and building out the foot geometry with ankle box and toe joints parented to the leg.

For the chain, I'll use leg.tip as the parenting point so the foot joint aims along the tangent naturally. Hands parent to arm.tip, and I'm setting up nine mohawk blades of varying sizes, drawn backward along the path with bones attached at each point.
